findings.text: Device memory control exposes region registration from a size descriptor plus formatted name with optional driver callbacks, and unregistration that detaches the region globally, releases member pools, blocks future pool creation, waits for readers, then drops its reference.

Charging resolves the current group pool for a region and attempts hierarchical accounting, transferring group ownership to the returned pool on success, while uncharge and pool release reverse accounting and drop group plus pool references.

Protection evaluation offers eviction permission checks and minimum plus low comparisons relative to an effective limit ancestor, recomputing hierarchical protection first, plus lookup of a shared ancestor pool for two pools.

Freezer control provides entry and exit handling for the frozen condition of the current task with hierarchical bookkeeping, plus a legacy query reporting whether a task resides under a freezing hierarchy.

Maximum updates become visible to concurrent allocators before any reclaim starts, so throttling never waits for eviction. Nonblocking callers return right after the update while blocking callers may then attempt reclaim.

Blocking limit reduction samples use and asks the region driver to free the excess until use fits, a signal is pending, a fatal driver error appears, or repeated no progress exhausts a bounded retry allowance, yielding between attempts and skipping when the region is gone or lacks reclaim.

Resource queries tolerate absent pools with defined fallbacks, yielding zero except for maximum which yields the unbounded sentinel, otherwise exposing live use with high watermark and configured protection values.

Group offline neutralizes every member pool by clearing protections and restoring unbounded maximum without sleeping. Final release unlinks plus destroys all member pools under exclusive lock before freeing the group object.

Pool creation binds one group to one region, inherits the parent group counter when present, starts with cleared protections and unbounded maximum, holds region plus parent references, joins group and region collections, and derives readiness from the parent.

Limit writes require a region name plus either the textual unbounded keyword or a numeric size, rejecting malformed text and unknown regions, then resolve the target pool and apply the value with blocking behavior derived from file flags.

Small freezer helpers translate hierarchy state into freezer records and derive task plus parent associations, tolerating absent input, while the legacy freezing test observes the combined freezing condition under read protection.

Pool and region collections are observed under read sections and mutated under a dedicated spinlock, with creation requiring that lock held. Limit reduction additionally holds a sleepable read section across driver reclaim, and unregistration detaches under the spinlock before waiting for that sleepable section.

Modern freezer transitions update frozen markers and counts under an interrupt safe hierarchy lock, briefly nesting the per task signal lock only to install a trap wakeup. Legacy hierarchy changes serialize under a dedicated mutex nested inside a CPU hotplug read section.

Each pool couples one group with one region, carrying hierarchical usage accounting with links to owning group and region plus optional parent pool, a readiness marker with private reference count, and membership nodes for group and region collections.

A region carries a name with total size, optional driver operations plus private reclaim context, a shared reference count with deferred release, a collection of member pools with global linkage, and a one way unregistered marker.
Legacy freezer state pairs hierarchy membership with a small bitmask recording online status alongside self freezing with parent freezing and fully frozen conditions.

The subsystem presents per region files for capacity alongside current use with peak and three tunable protections, with capacity restricted to the root and peak plus tunables excluded from the root, served from one shared table for both hierarchy versions.

Regions progress from allocated to globally visible, then on unregistration to detached plus unregistered with pools released, followed by a grace interval before final destruction of pools with name storage and descriptor.

Pools start unready during recursive creation along ancestors, then gain parent linkage and become ready from ancestor toward descendant, with fast lookup ignoring unready entries and slow creation completing the chain before returning.

Legacy groups start thawed, become online on attachment inheriting freezing plus frozen when the parent is freezing, may acquire self freezing with frozen while active, and on detach clear all state and release active tracking if freezing was set.

Group lifecycle enters through allocation of an empty pool collection with offline neutralization of limits and final destruction of pools, while user control enters through show routines listing every region and write routines dispatching to the matching protection setter.

Legacy hierarchy lifecycle enters through allocation of an empty state object with online marking ready and inheriting parent freezing plus active tracking, offline clearing state and tracking, and final release of the object.

Pool resolution retries allocation outside the spinlock using a preallocated spare, warns on unexpected spare retention, distinguishes exhaustion from use of a dead region, and never attaches new pools to an unregistered region.

Failed hierarchical charging reports contention distinctly and may pin the limiting ancestor for caller driven reclaim, while stale handles are discarded safely and successful charging keeps group plus pool pinned until explicit uncharge.

Region lookup by name with pool fast lookup only return objects whose reference could be acquired safely, unregistration waits out sleepable readers before dropping the final reference, and region destruction defers pool plus name release through a grace period.

Entering frozen state is idempotent for an already frozen task. Leaving validates the frozen marker and either fully clears it or installs a trap wakeup when the hierarchy remains freezing, with misuse surfaced through a one time warning.

User visible names include capacity and current and peak and min and low and max, with capacity limited to the root and peak plus min plus low plus max excluded from the root, terminated by an empty entry.

Legacy status uses four distinct low bits for online and self freezing and parent freezing and fully frozen, treats both freezing bits as one combined freezing condition, and displays FROZEN with precedence over FREEZING over THAWED.
The textual unbounded keyword maps to the maximal counter sentinel, numeric sizes require strict full string consumption, and display prints the keyword whenever a stored value reaches that sentinel.
